P1.evidence: No setter code on the title and no setter involved, so the read-back is N/A. The frame was the rep's standard two-part version: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, and then build out what it is that you want, what you want to accomplish, and then if everything aligns, we can talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine as well.' No 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement requested and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Okay.'), and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The health half ran well. The back was probed directly and specifically — 'you said some back stuff. What's kind of been going on now?' — which produced the chiropractic management, the occupational trigger and the multi-year duration. Training status was asked ('Are you training right now, or no?'). Weight was asked as an interest question rather than a measurement — 'In terms of weights, are you bothered by that at all? Is there any weight you need to lose or any weight you want to gain?' — which got 225 lb and six foot, but age was never asked. Occupation came out because the prospect volunteered it while explaining his back; the rep only confirmed ownership at 00:23:34, after quoting the price, and used it to open the tax write-off angle rather than to qualify. Diet was never asked directly; the keto history was volunteered. Results from current training, sleep and daytime energy were never touched, and energy is one of the outcomes he named himself.

P3.evidence: The reflect-back is the best single move in the batch and it is worth preserving: 'I want to summarize. It sounds like the things that are important to you... firstly, something that's sustainable. Secondly, something safe, you don't want to be getting injured. Thirdly, something that allows you to bond. Fourthly, something that allows you to lose the weight whilst also getting stronger. Something you can easily ingrain as a habit into your lifestyle. Is there anything else there that you feel like is important?' — confirmed with 'that pretty much nails it.' But it summarised material the prospect had volunteered rather than material the rep had excavated. The deep questions never ran: no bridge to what is actually driving this outside the physical, no 'when you're moving better, what does that do for you', and critically no 'who else does that impact' — the son, the homeschooling gap and the soccer both arrived unprompted. The role-model thread was asserted back rather than asked for: 'We want to hold you accountable to the version of you who is the role model for his kids.'

P4.evidence: The strongest past-attempts work in the batch. The root-cause question was asked properly and with a stated reason: 'For you, in your opinion, when you start and then the consistency drops off, what have you noticed is typically like a reason why that would happen? Or like a pattern... because I want to make sure that that's the biggest thing that we're fixing as well.' The prospect had genuinely not considered it ('I don't know that I've really thought about it that way') and then named his own gap precisely — travel and disrupted routine, and the compounding of missed days. The rep probed once more with a hypothesis about self-blame, which the prospect corrected, and accepted the correction. What did not run: what have you tried and what happened with it were never asked (the keto history was volunteered), and the closing move — 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' — was never delivered, even though the prospect had already answered it unprompted: 'building out a training program is just not really my skillset... I don't have a whole lot of capacity for right now.'

P5.evidence: No consequence frame ran. The prospect built one himself and handed it over — 'I'd prefer to not spend a bunch of money in the future in healthcare stuff because I'm not taking care of myself now either' — and the rep's only use of it was a one-line price pre-empt fifteen minutes later, 'It'll be cheaper than surgery in 10 years if you needed it.' Nothing about the next two years, no test of willingness to settle, no 'why not', no line in the sand, on a prospect who had just said 'I feel like I'm losing that day by day.'

P6.evidence: A process check stood in for the belief question and got a soft yes: 'How do you feel about it in terms of the process?' — 'it sounds good. It sounds like what I would like to do, for sure.' The all-in question did eventually run, and ran well, but reactively and after the price and the spouse objection: 'if you have that conversation, she's like, yeah, all good — is it something that you want to do most importantly?' followed by 'Are you sure? I just want to make sure.' Run before the number, that same question would have surfaced Lauren pre-price. Credit for returning to commitment before proceeding rather than plunging on.

P11.evidence: Payment was collected, but only the $100 refundable hold, not the programme fee — 'I'm just going to put a Stripe link in the chat for you for the hundred bucks' / 'Yeah, I just paid it just now.' The Trevor onboarding call was described and indicated for Monday or Tuesday but never booked; what was booked was a follow-up with the rep at 4pm the next day. No agreement email, no signature on the call, and no welcome email, Skool link or onboarding questionnaire instruction, all of which correctly wait on the full payment.

objection_plays.detail: The only objection play in the batch played through to its scripted terminal move. Trigger at 00:24:29. Ran: asked her name to personalise it ('What's your wife's name? I don't want to call her your wife' — 'Lauren'), asked whether she is supportive of the journey, established she had not been told anything yet, ran the two-reactions framing to elicit the likely obstacle ('How do you feel like she would react to that?' — 'the money piece of it would be probably the biggest sticking point'), isolated personal commitment twice, and then closed the scripted fallback exactly as written: a refundable deposit with a full refund if she says no, plus a booked follow-up. The prospect paid it inside a minute. Not run: 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', the permission-versus-input challenge, and the 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' ownership move — reasonably omitted given the prospect framed the decision in explicitly joint and faith terms.

Soft money trigger at 00:15:43 ('money is always a question, so that's always a huge piece'), raised before any number existed. The rep answered with a single cost-of-inaction line — 'It'll be cheaper than surgery in 10 years if you needed it' — and later with the business write-off angle. Neither is in the play. No isolation, no 'HOW place' reframe, no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions. It resolved anyway because the prospect talked himself into it ('six grand seems like a drop in the bucket over the long haul'), which is the prospect doing the rep's work, not the play running.

Script gap — clinical fit. The prospect disclosed multi-year recurrent lower back episodes under active chiropractic care, with acute flare-ups triggered by lifting, and stated his current strategy is avoidance. The rep asked good discovery questions about it and then routed the entire clinical question to post-purchase: 'If you can give us a lot of data or things that the chiropractor said about X, Y and Z, that information's super key.' Between those two points he guaranteed an eight-kilogram load increase on every movement. The script has no clearance gate, so nothing stopped that sequence.

notes: The rep's best call in the batch on objection handling — the spouse play ran nearly in full and terminated correctly in a paid refundable deposit with a next-day follow-up booked, which is exactly what the playbook asks for. The process gaps are the same as everywhere else: no consequence frame, and the all-in question asked reactively after the price instead of before it. One thing to stop immediately, unrelated to selling: do not offer to help clients structure a personal coaching purchase as a business tax write-off.
